source.text: ውእተ፡ ጊዜ፡ አውሥአኒ፡ ኡርኤል፡ ፩*እምቅዱሳን፡ መላእክት፡ እንዘ፡ ምስሌየ፡ ሀሎ፡ ወይቤለኒ፡ ሄኖክ፡ ምንት፡ ፍርሃትከ፡ ከመዝ፡ ወድንጋጼከ፡ ወአውሣእኩ፡ በእንተዝ፡ ግሩም፡ መካን፡ ወቅድመ፡ ገጹ፡ *ለዝ፡ ሕማም፡፡
source.note: Selected Charles1906 printed54-56/PDF92-94. Complete cross-page 21:9 with asterisk before እምቅዱሳን and terminal ፡፡. Answer verb follows printed editorial restoration explained by p55 note46; no independent manuscript claim.

translation.text: At that time Uriel, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered me and said, “Enoch, why are you so afraid and alarmed?” And I answered[a], “Because of this terrifying place and the sight of this suffering[b].”

footnotes.text: Charles 1906 printed p56 note4 identifies the answer verb as restored and refers to p55 note46. Note46 says it was wrongly transposed into the earlier clause; Charles restores ወአውሣእኩ after ወድንጋጼከ, at the end of Uriel’s question. This follows the editor’s placement, not independent manuscript attestation there.

The phrase literally refers to being before the face of this pain or suffering. Charles page 56 note 5 contrasts the printed Ethiopic with the Greek. Sight is contextual and no bodily torment mechanism is specified.
